patch.description:
Opt in to (or out of) nudge emails: a reminder when you haven't stored a card in a while. Opting in shares
your handle, role and email with the team's mailing list.

get.description: Everyone on the team, the people waiting to be let in first.

delete.description:
Removes someone from the team: their account is closed and every sign-in revoked at once. Their
handle stays reserved, since commits they made carry it.

post.description: Let someone in: they see the team's work from their next request. Turning someone away is removing them.

Signed in: add a passkey to this account. Signed out, with a handle and an invite: create an
account whose first sign-in method is this passkey (the invite is used up when it is verified).
Add or change the account's email + password. Changing one needs the current password.

delete.description: No more notifications in this browser.

get.description: `topic`, `file` and `block` filter by slug and name, as the apps know them.

delete.description: Archive: the file is deleted in a commit; history keeps every version.

get.description: Cards whose files link to this one.

post.description: Model suggestions are pending spans in the index; accepting one commits it to the card file.

With `content`, commit sources/<n>.md as sent. With only `url`, the server reads the article
and commits its clean text.

A photo of a printed card, read by OCR on this server into a draft: `tag`, `cite`, `body`, `text` (all three:
what becomes the source), `markdown`, and `spans`: the underlines, highlights and emphasis read off the paper, over
`body`. With `quad` (a JSON list of 8 numbers: the card's corners, TL TR BR BL, in the photo the app took), the
photo must be the app's warp of those corners to the card's flat frame; it's then also turned upright. The photo
is read in memory and never stored: no file, row or commit, and only the text goes back.

get.description: Your scans waiting to be checked, newest first. Drafts left untouched for 30 days are dropped.

delete.description: Discard a draft, or clear it once its card is saved.

patch.description:
Fix the tag or cite, or mark the words: `spans` replaces the draft's marks (underline, highlight, emphasis over
`body`, UTF-16 offsets on whole characters). The words themselves stay as read: the card keeps them exactly.

post.description:
A photo of paper at any angle, as the camera took it. This server finds the card's four corners, squares the
card up (undoing its tilt toward the camera), turns it upright and reads it into a draft to check, as
/scan/screenshot, plus `corners`: where it found them, as fractions of the upright photo (TL TR BR BL, x y). Send
`corners` (a JSON list of 8 such fractions) with `replaces` to read it again from corners the member dragged.

A scan that failed on the member's phone before it reached /scan (the camera, the scanner script, the picture,
or the upload): `step` where, `message` what the phone said, `agent` its browser. Written to this server's log
only, so the team's operator can see a failure that never left the phone.

A screenshot, read as it is (no corners, no turning, lossless), into a draft to check: `id`, `kind`, `tag`,
`cite`, `body`, `text`, `markdown`, `spans`. A picture a camera took is read as a photo instead, and `kind` says
`photo`. `replaces`: one of your drafts this reads again (200 instead of 201). The picture isn't kept.

get.description:
Cards: `q` is Google's syntax ("a phrase", -word, a OR b; the last word matches as a prefix while it's being
typed), matched in tiers: the phrase, then every word, then any word. `sort=best` orders by tier, then
rank; `recent` by the last change; `published` by the source's date, newest first. `month` (2024-03) keeps cards
whose source was published that month.

Every card that quotes or names a person: cards whose words name them (spaCy's PERSON names; the surname alone
counts) and cards cut from a source they wrote. Names match ignoring case and "Last, First" order.

config.cfg + train.spacy + dev.spacy, ready for `python -m spacy train config.cfg
--paths.train train.spacy --paths.dev dev.spacy`.
Topics you have cards under first, then custom ones, then newest seasons.
